summary: Move the existing 84/46 request-granting example to II.2.
rationale: The speaker asks for an unspecified favour with beneficiary -li and b-matter; forgiveness of a fault is not at issue.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (JTM 3.2/43)
rationale: New II Part act. box; habitual forgiving disposition with dayəm and howe.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Story of Dawid/22)

data.turoyo: Aṯi qolo mu+qawro, omar, ‘Mšiḥo msamaḥ’. Háwoste lo+kәmsamàḥwayle.
data.translation: A voice came from the grave, it says, ‘It is Christ who forgives’. As for that one, he wasn’t forgiving him.

rationale: New II Infectum-wa box; explicit past refusal contrasts with generic forgiveness in the same two-sentence context.

summary: New sense 2: (mit l-: jdm.; b-: etw.) eine Bitte gewähren, etw. erlauben

data.gloss: (mit l-: jdm.; b-: etw.) eine Bitte gewähren, etw. erlauben

rationale: 84/46 asks for a future favour with beneficiary -li and matter ebe; there is no wrongdoing to forgive. The sentence is already present under forgiveness and needs its own sense, distinct from but related to I erlauben.

data.turoyo: Aloho lə ksoməḥ l ənsan d howe bi ḥkumayḏe w howe kin w ġaraz b lebe
data.translation: Gott erlaubt es dem Menschen nicht, dass er unter seiner Regierung lebt und (zugleich) in seinem Herzen Hass und Rachegedanken (gegen andere) hegt.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; overt l-person and finite content clause.

data.turoyo: Ṭabʕan, i kačke aʕmi yo. Kobaʕno d səmḥatli, d mobannola, hul d mḥaḏ̣rinala
data.translation: Das Mädchen ist natürlich bei mir. Ich bitte dich, mir zu erlauben, daß ich es mitnehme, bis wir sie bereitgemacht haben.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; beneficiary -li and permission for an explicit action.

data.turoyo: Məllela: "Mə kəbʕat?" Əmmo: "Kəbʕono, d səmḥatli, d kəṯwono maktub l Ṭahər Bag, d oṯelux nažda musaʕade.
data.translation: Er sprach zu ihr: "Was willst du?" Sie sprach: "Du sollst mir erlauben, daß ich Tahir Bäg einen Brief schreibe, daß er dir zu Hilfe kommen soll.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; permission to write a letter, complete request context.

summary: I permits conduct with a personal l- complement and content clause; II usually forgives a personal object, including direct suffixes, with b- optionally naming the fault (36/138). The same formal b- can instead name the requested matter in new II.2, so role and context matter.
Active II with ḥḏoḏe in 42/10–11 expresses mutual forgiveness without a Detransitive stem. The first/second plural change follows the quoted speaker and addressee.

Generic and optative bare Infectum, performative Infectum, past continuing refusal in Infectum-wa and habitual Part act. are distinct contextual uses of the inherited forgiveness meaning. Christ/God as forgiver is not a new sense.
The Arabic derivation is retained; this is a lexical verb rather than a light-verb construction. No new idiom is proposed.
Confirm the predicate msamḥono as Part act. rather than a separately lexicalised dispositional adjective; dayəm and howe motivate the proposed filing.
Clarify who says 'uncle' to whom in MAC NE Story of Dawid/23. The quotation boundaries do not establish the referents; this does not affect the forgiveness sense.
Confirm whether permission/granting II.2 is productive beyond the single 84/46 request.
